text:
maria: quick follow-up from the RFC thread — we still don't have a clear convergence criteria for the prober handshake. bench-fuzz is surfacing a bunch of flaky passes. do we codify a pass rule or keep the current heuristic?

sam: agree we should codify. heuristics are biting us in prod. my vote: require both a statistical pass and a golden-probe agreement.

alex: +1. suggestion: two checks — (1) pass_rate >= 0.95 over N samples, (2) delta vs golden median latency within 10% and output similarity >= 0.98 (embedding cosine).

rui: curious about N. 100 samples might be too small for heavy-tail latency distributions. suggest stratified sampling across seq-lens: short/medium/long buckets, N_per_bucket = 50.

josh: sounds reasonable. also we need a handshake timeout: if probe doesn't converge in T=30m, we mark warmup-failed and route to fallback. avoid indefinite retries.

maria: ok — so far: stratified sample, pass_rate >=95% per bucket, golden agreement threshold, and a 30m handshake timeout. what about flaky outputs from stochastic sampling? we should use deterministic seeds for probes.

sam: yes — run probes with fixed seed and temperature=0 for content checks. keep a separate stochastic smoke-run for real-world behavior, but deterministic for gating.

alex: telemetry bits: emit metric `onboard.prober.pass_rate` per bucket, `onboard.prober.latency_p50`/p95, `onboard.prober.embedding_sim` vs golden. these drive alerts/rollbacks.

rui: one edge-case: kv-cache priming changes latency dramatically. probe should include a priming phase: e.g., 10 prefix runs to fill kv cache before measuring. document as `priming_runs=10` in prober config.

josh: and add a small synthetic load test for batching effects — measure throughput at target qps to catch queuing regressions. this can run after handshake; it's heavier but catches regressions that single-request probes miss.

maria: draft of a simple accept rule (pseudocode):

```
for bucket in buckets:
  samples = run_probes(bucket, seeds=fixed, priming=10)
  if pass_rate(samples) < 0.95:
    reject
  if embedding_sim_median(samples, golden) < 0.98:
    reject
if all buckets pass and latency_ok:
  mark_accepted
else:
  reject
```

sam: two practical asks: (1) log full sample diffs for failed admits (for triage), (2) store a minimal golden snapshot with S3 path + hash for reproducibility.

alex: on storage — keep a versioned golden per model-version and per-quantization-profile. otherwise small kernel changes will make comparisons noisy.

rui: operational note: prober should support `fallthrough` policy: if a model fails admit but a compatible lower-capacity variant exists, route can opt-in to fallback instead of full reject. this reduces customer outages.

maria: can we make that a config flag on the model manifest? `admit_policy: {require_pass: bool, allow_fallback: bool, fallback_model: id}`

josh: yep. add a canary window too: after accept, route 1% traffic for 1h before full promotion. tie canary metrics to the same prober signals.

ci-bot: reminder — please update the RFC doc: https://redwood/s/rfcs/model-onboard-prober (bot)

maria: thanks — i'll update the RFC with the proposed criteria and action items: add priming_runs, stratified N_per_bucket=50, pass_rate=0.95, embed_sim=0.98, deterministic seeds, priming + small batch throughput test, handshake_timeout=30m, and fallthrough flag. assigning follow-ups: sam (triage logs), alex (telemetry + metrics), rui (priming + sampling), josh (fallback policy + canary).

sam: great. i'll prototype the failing-sample dump format (JSONL with input, output, embedding, latency).

alex: i'll add dashboards and new metrics events.

rui: i'll sketch priming and sampling config.

josh: i'll write fallback + canary config examples.

maria: perfect — if nobody objects i'll fold this into the RFC by end of week. :thumbsup:
